title: Low's handwritten note: Hippler blames EMP from nuclear testing

Colonel Robert Hiper is saying that this was due to a, you know, an EMP fallout from a nuclear detonation,
tellings.difference: Comes through the 2025 Wall Street Journal article rather than Low's handwritten 1967 note.
tellings.link_reason: Both attribute the missile shutdown to Colonel Robert Hippler blaming EMP from nuclear testing or detonation.

plain: The story is that in 1967 an Air Force colonel privately offered an explanation for a UFO incident: that it was caused by fallout from a nuclear blast. It turns on a handwritten note by Robert Low, a figure at the Condon Committee, a UFO study the Air Force paid the University of Colorado to run in the late 1960s. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer who says a UFO shut down ten nuclear missiles he was guarding, tells Michels about this note. He says Low wrote that he had talked to Colonel Robert Hippler and that Hippler told him something. Michels gives the content. He says Hippler put the event down to an EMP, an electromagnetic pulse, from a nuclear detonation. Michels gets this from a Wall Street Journal article, "The Pentagon Disinformation That Fueled America's UFO Mythology", published on 6 June 2025, rather than from the note itself. Salas raises it because, if true, the note would show the Air Force had an explanation ready for the incident.
